name: Turnwisee
audience: People who enjoy small visual puzzles, spatial reasoning, clever objects and satisfying transformations. The story must be understandable across languages and while muted. Start with objects, materials and mechanisms; this is an audience hypothesis, not a claim of universal appeal. General audience, not specifically directed at children.
concept:
Small mysteries. Clever transformations. Satisfying endings. Visual stories told without words — made to spark curiosity wherever you are. No talking. Just a closer look.

The Turnwise promise: one clearly visible question, real progress and an honest answer in every episode. Change the viewer's understanding with a turn, a reveal or a transformation. Start with three series: WILL IT WORK? (fitting and mechanisms), WHAT IS IT? (macro clues and a complete reveal), and FLAT TO FORM (material transformations). Each episode stands alone.

Identity: warm brass #dba04f, porcelain #ece8d9 and deep teal #1e353c. A tilted element passing through a ring is the profile mark. Brand primarily through consistent craft, lighting and object relationships, not an opening logo. Metadata in natural English; the film itself needs no language.

Pilot: The long way through — an original 22-second 3D visual story. A long brass capsule cannot pass sideways through a smaller circular opening. It rises onto its end, aligns, passes continuously through and settles on the lower tray. A fixed solid shape and engraved bands preserve identity. This is stylized authored animation, not documentary footage or a validated physics experiment.

Editorial v2 (15 September 2026): make the visible problem and its consequence interesting before polishing the image. Prefer active mechanisms, functional transformations and recognisable parts in action. Choose a solution worth discovering; movement should have an understandable cause. Physics is a useful production method for dynamics stories, not a guaranteed source of engagement.
rules:
EDITORIAL CONTRACT
1. One question, one story, one satisfying solution.
2. The film works without dialogue, a title or sound.
3. Every interval changes the object, understanding or expectation; shorten repetition and waiting.
4. Every source has recorded provenance and cleared scope; every episode has a distinct authored contribution.
5. Repeat the viewer benefit, not an identical template. Grow volume only after quality and series evidence support it.

GENERATION V2 — 15 SEPTEMBER 2026
Before any full render, read examples/turnwise/GENERATION_RULES.md. Prepare three brief candidates, choose one with reasons and make a low-cost storyboard or animatic. Gate the idea on six conditions: a visible goal and obstacle; a plausible viewer prediction or concrete question with uncertainty about how or whether the goal will be achieved; a visible cause for each important motion; meaningful progress; a complete demonstrated solution; and a mechanism that can actually be generated and verified. An attractive image or score cannot compensate for a failed condition. A simple 90-degree turn of a floating rod is not a sufficient next episode. Record editorial_version: 2 and the evidence.
Build dynamics from events, not stimulus count. Show a readable situation with tension or preparatory motion immediately; show the full problem from frame one and release a simple readable mechanism around 1.0 s. Do not impose a 2–3 s wait; context and an opportunity to predict still precede the decisive trigger. Remove extended movement that adds no information. These are editorial heuristics, not platform rules. Use the duration required by meaningful events and a readable payoff; the approved 10 s episode 003 is a valid compact story. Earlier 12–17 s and 18–24 s ranges are optional guides for richer stories, not minimum lengths. Never slow physics or pad a film to reach a duration. Show the payoff promptly once the answer becomes clear, with 1–3 s to appreciate it.
For falling, rolling, impacts, balance and lever stories, test a simulation or valid computational model before visual polish. Retain geometry, units, masses, gravity, friction, restitution, constraints, initial conditions, time step and engine/model version. Inspect fast contacts for tunnelling. No hidden forces or manual steering after release to manufacture success. A scripted geometric mechanism is acceptable when its cause is explicit; disclose animation honestly and do not call a successful model a proven real-world experiment.
The next three new episodes are an exploratory v2 cohort. The lever-and-ball concept was produced as episode 002; inspect existing episode state and do not recreate it as a new episode. Scheduled production remains authorized. Keep the existing cadence and target mix of three series. Compare comparable-age results by editorial version, series and length. Multiple concurrent creative changes are not an isolated physics A/B test; no claim of improvement from a single episode.

OPENING CLARIFICATION — 15 SEPTEMBER 2026
Show the full problem before the decisive action: the object's starting position, relevant route and obstacles, destination, and any weight, spring or actuator needed to understand the cause. The first frame already communicates the full relationship. For a simple readable setup, release around 1.0 s as in approved episode 003. The earlier 2–3 s reading window is flexible for more complex context, not a mandatory pause. Simplify an overcomplicated setup instead of extending a camera tour. The viewer should be able to form either a plausible prediction or a specific question. A correct prediction can be satisfying; a twist is not mandatory.
Show the conditions, not the completed answer: visible rails or gaps invite prediction, but do not pre-draw the exact successful flight trajectory or conceal the force that explains success. Compose the mechanism compactly or vertically for 9:16; do not shrink a wide machine until it becomes unreadable. Establish orientation before close-ups. Macro may withhold object identity while retaining an understandable action and question.
Before full rendering, inspect the opening at about 360 px width, muted and title-free. Freeze just before the actual decisive trigger, e.g. at 0.9 s for a 1.0 s release, and identify the start, obstacle, target and plausible prediction/question without later-shot knowledge. Failure requires a revised storyboard, framing or geometry. Record editorial_version: 2, opening_variant: full_problem_first, the time context becomes complete and the trigger time. This is an agent editorial check, not a claimed human audience test.

LOOP RESTART CLARIFICATION — OWNER REQUEST, 15 SEPTEMBER 2026
For a looping construction, start the decisive release around 200 ms from the beginning, superseding the default one-second opening for ordinary standalone stories. Assess the ending plus the beginning as one continuous interval: waiting after the returning object settles and waiting before its next release must not accumulate into a long inactive pause. The opening frame still shows the full problem for a first-time viewer. Prefer trimming an unnecessary lead-in, synchronously on picture and all audio, instead of accelerating physics or weakening the payoff. Preserve the continuous return and inspect two consecutive playbacks. Record loop_restart_delay_ms and the combined end/start pacing check.
Episode 003 now applies this as a trim only: remove the first 800 ms of the 10 s fast-loop source; current duration 9.2 s, release at 0.2 s. Project 509271541ff442e9bb82a2bc49396f65, revision 16, render f17678ad856e4f8faece8ca7fe996acb; source edit and QA in examples/turnwise/episodes/003-missing-track/fast-loop/trim-200ms/. Earlier 10 s references remain the historical tempo approval. When monitoring performance, confirm the actual published variant and video ID; do not assume the public video was replaced.

OWNER-APPROVED MOTION AND OPTIONAL LOOP — 15 SEPTEMBER 2026
Standing tempo reference: episode 003, Two gaps. One ball., fast-loop variant, 10 s; project 509271541ff442e9bb82a2bc49396f65, revision 7, render 1537ed5017fe428e83ed11f3eba4b94e. Full source and QA: examples/turnwise/episodes/003-missing-track/fast-loop/. These rules supersede older slow-motion, delayed-release and minimum-duration suggestions.
Default to real-time physics at 1.0x with the lively, readable pace of this approved version. Do not routinely slow the whole simulation to 0.30x or 0.38x. Brief slow motion is an exception only for an important otherwise unreadable contact; record the reason and return to normal time. Do not copy one metres-per-second value to every mechanism. Set scale, geometry and energy before simulation; keep natural acceleration, contacts and deceleration. No hidden impulse or free-flight steering to manufacture pace. Review the full playback for monotony: no slow drifting, uniform easing or long repetition of the same movement. Shorten empty preparation or change the course before production; a 1.0x label alone does not pass the tempo check.
A natural loop is a desirable effect when supported by the story, not a requirement for every episode. Show the complete solution first and let the viewer read it before the return. The payoff can remain visible during preparation of the reset, without a frozen end card. A caught ball can visibly launch and return with the camera to the same start. Preserve object identity, continuous motion and the visible source of reset energy, including recharging a spring; do not imply perpetual motion. No teleport, hidden substitution, black-frame reset or rewind masking a failed ending. If the return adds dead time or requires cheating, use an ordinary satisfying ending.
Review two consecutive playbacks for matching object position and motion, mechanism state, camera framing, lighting and audio across the boundary. Repeat a satisfying viewer experience, not the identical course in every upload. Record motion_preset: realtime, the actual simulation-time multiplier, justified slow-motion exceptions, loop_type: none or causal_return, payoff/return times and evidence of tempo and seam checks.
Owner approval establishes an editorial preference, not audience-performance evidence. During the existing evening automation on 16 September 2026, inspect this variant only after confirming its actual YouTube video ID and publication time; otherwise mark evaluation as awaiting publication. Record actual age, available public metrics and Studio viewing/retention data. A 10 s loop is not directly comparable to a 22 s or 13.5 s film; higher APV alone does not establish satisfaction or the causal benefit of a loop. Follow later 24 h, 72 h, 7 d and 28 d observations under YOUTUBE_EXPERIMENT.md.

STORY DESIGN
Design backward from a complete final reveal. Record the question, opening frame, necessary progress beats, solution, original contribution and asset list before assembly. Let the necessary events determine length; a complete 10 s story is welcome. Earlier 12–17 s and 18–24 s ranges guide richer stories without setting a minimum. Longer processes must justify their additional necessary stages. These are production starting ranges, not algorithmic requirements. A 24-second outline is optional: immediate obstacle, short attempt, meaningful change, final clue, answer and brief satisfaction. Do not pad a simpler idea to match it. Keep cause and effect truthful; do not combine different processes and imply continuity.

SOUND AND TEXT
No dialogue, narration or TTS. No burned-in explanations or language-dependent title requirements. Build the muted cut first. Add restrained licensed or original sound afterward, on separate editable tracks. Do not assume platform audio rights transfer. Measure the rendered mix and avoid clipping; do not claim subjective listening from a meter. End all tracks with the picture.

SOURCES AND RIGHTS
Prefer original or commissioned sequences. Other candidates: verified public domain, CC0, CC BY or suitable stock licenses, with author, exact source URL, acquisition date, license text/evidence, permitted adaptations/platforms/commercial use, restrictions and required attribution recorded per asset. Unknown means unresolved. Escalate NC, ND, ShareAlike, editorial-only or unclear permissions for specific evaluation before use. Sound needs its own record. Stock is an ingredient, not a ready episode. A download, permission, logo or amount of editing does not itself establish originality or monetization eligibility. Never invent a rights confirmation. Preserve all required attributions. For code-created work, retain source code, render parameters, file hashes and truthful production provenance; do not pretend it is a filmed physical event.

RELEASE GATE
Require source clearance, substantial authorship, wordless comprehension, honest continuity, an actual visible payoff and technical review. Run preflight, render, inspect real opening/progress/critical transition/final frames and full decode; record the exact project revision and job. Check actual audio where present. The owner authorized ongoing production and publication on 14 September 2026 through the evening automation. A separate owner approval is not required for each compliant episode. Agent editorial review, actual-export QA and target-platform safe-area review precede publishing. Periodic muted/title-free comprehension checks with people remain useful; record unperformed human checks as pending and never claim they occurred. An agent may publish a compliant episode under this standing authorization but may not invent human approval, analytics or listening. Actual tool approval requirements still apply.

INTERNAL RUBRIC
Opening 20 + clarity 20 + progression 20 + ending 25 + technical craft 15. Aim for 80/100 only after all release gates are met. This is subjective editorial scoring, never a viral prediction. Synkinema's five-field channel review uses a different rubric: identify that distinction instead of equating its score with this one.

METADATA
Natural English, usually 4–8 title words / about 20–55 characters, accurate to the actual film. Unique description of one or two sentences, required source/license/change and audio credits, optionally 0–3 relevant lowercase hashtags. No false statistics, all-caps bait, 'wait for it' or promises of guaranteed reach. Describe original animation as animation. Platform/model disclosure requirements must be checked at publication; no invented account URLs or publication records.

ACTIVE EVENING EXPERIMENT — OWNER AUTHORIZED 14 SEPTEMBER 2026
Six episodes per week at most, Monday–Saturday, one public film per local day; Sunday analysis only. Active heartbeat: Turnwisee — analiza, produkcja i publikacja. Daily 18:30 Europe/Warsaw: analyze, produce and review one new episode on publication days. Daily 21:30: publish a ready draft or confirm its scheduled publication and collect measurements. No automated work from 06:00 to 18:00; stop by 05:30. Respect owner UI activity. Do not duplicate existing public, scheduled or private uploads; resume recorded work. Skip a slot if quality or tool checks cannot be completed.
First 12 episodes: four from each of three series; use v2 duration guidance and record actual length and editorial version. Series order may change after concept review. Compare similarly aged results after all 12 reach seven days; if the choice is inconclusive, extend the test. Then test length in the selected format, changing one variable at a time. Keep the publication time at 21:30; the earlier 13:00/19:00 UTC comparison is deferred. No autonomous cadence increase. Procedures and decision rules: examples/turnwise/AUTOMATION.md and YOUTUBE_EXPERIMENT.md. Public metrics use the configured read-only YouTube MCP; uploads use authorized logged-in Studio access. Preserve actual publication IDs, timestamps, project revisions, QA and source provenance.

MEASUREMENT
Keep YouTube and TikTok separate. Record observations at 24 h, 72 h, 7 d and 28 d with source and timestamp. Compare similar-age, similar-length videos and traffic sources; compare series medians. Track choose-to-watch/swipe, engaged views, average duration/percentage, retention curve, shares, follows and return viewers when actually available. Public plays, engaged views and completion are distinct. Replays can indicate delight or confusion. Diagnose weak openings, stalls and delayed payoffs as hypotheses. No universal viral percentage thresholds. Leave unknown metrics blank. Short episodes are not designed around a minute-plus rewards program. Verify current platform rules before relevant publication or monetization decisions.

WORKSPACE
Keep the linked Synkinema timeline editable, preserve other channels/projects/media, use server-confirmed revisions, and retain source and QA files. Standing owner authorization covers production and publication of compliant episodes on @turnwisee through the evening automation. It does not authorize purchases, paid ads, new subscriptions, additional credits, unrelated account changes or bypassing tool approvals.
tone: Curious, precise, warm and quietly playful. Let viewers notice the solution. Restrained tactile sound design; no dialogue, voiceover, robotic announcements, artificial urgency or sensory overload. V2: give motion weight, visible causes and purposeful tempo; quiet means restrained sound, not a uniformly slow or weightless animation.
hook_guidance:
The first frame already contains the object and its goal or obstacle. Reveal context immediately and withhold only the answer. Make the scale or relationship readable on a phone. No black intro, logo animation, title card, long camera approach, 'wait for it' or intentionally incomprehensible macro. A short failed attempt may establish the rule; do not repeat equivalent failures just to add time.

V2 / full_problem_first: show the starting object, relevant route, obstacle, destination and necessary cause of motion before the decisive trigger. The opening frame communicates the full relationship. For a simple readable mechanism release around 1.0 s, as in approved episode 003. The earlier 2–3 s reading window is flexible, not a required delay. Meaningful tension can begin immediately; clarity still precedes the decisive trigger. Let the viewer form either a plausible prediction or a concrete question. A correct prediction is welcome; a twist is optional. Show the course, not a preview of the exact successful flight path. Establish orientation before close-ups; no static intro or long camera tour. A beauty shot, an object merely beside a hole, or a barely visible contact does not establish enough tension. Check the first 3 s at roughly 360 px width with sound and title absent. Write what the viewer predicts and why they still need the answer. For macro stories, show understandable behaviour of a part; do not begin with an unreadable texture.
Before full rendering, freeze the muted, title-free opening before the decisive trigger and record the start, obstacle, target and prediction/question. If later footage is needed to explain these, revise the opening. Record opening_variant: full_problem_first, context-complete time and trigger time.
Loop-specific override: when the ending returns to the opening setup, release around 0.20 s, not after another full second. Read the last and first moments as one continuous interval and remove duplicated waiting. The first frame must still show the full problem for a first-time viewer.
cta_guidance: Complete the answer before any invitation. No spoken CTA, burned-in question, subscription card or unresolved part two. A 1–3 second clear result is the default ending. A natural loop is optional and may never hide the payoff. An optional specific question can live in the publication description after its unique summary, but the episode must work without reading it.
visual_guidance:
9:16, 1080 × 1920, 30 fps; clean full-frame exports. One main object relationship with a readable background, warm material contrast and purposeful motion. No subtitles are needed when there is no speech. Avoid platform chrome, letterboxing and intrusive watermarks. Keep crucial action away from the right control rail and bottom description; review each target platform preview before publication.

Use continuous motion when it proves the mechanism. Cuts must reveal new information. Do not morph a rigid object, change an opening's size, teleport through an obstruction or swap the final object to manufacture a solution. Stylized animation is allowed and must be described honestly. Hold the final state long enough to understand. Sound is supplementary: restrained clicks, rubbing and movement accents. Optional music has no vocals. No narrative dependency on a trending sound.

V2: dynamics should arise from contact, gravity, load, a hinge, spring or visible actuator. Use a tested simulation or computational model when the story promises physical behaviour; preserve parameters and reproducible initial conditions. Test collisions, constraints and the full free-motion trajectory before the polished render. Do not guide a released object invisibly into its target, animate massless floating, invent impulses, or use rigid bodies to claim material-strength results. Authored geometric animation remains appropriate when its actuator or transformation is clear.
Establish the readable start–route/obstacle–destination layout before decisive action and before close-ups. Include the trigger or energy source when needed to predict the result. Design a compact, preferably vertical mechanism for 9:16; do not shrink a wide apparatus to an unreadable miniature. Keep essential relationships legible at about 360 px width. Show the physical course without drawing the exact winning flight trajectory in advance. Vary motion through causal acceleration, contact and brief anticipation. A slow camera orbit or another angle is not itself narrative progress. Inspect intervals longer than about 2 s without new information and shorten or justify them; no mandatory cut frequency. Keep a complete 1–3 s payoff.
Owner-approved tempo reference: episode 003 fast-loop, revision 7, 10 s. Default physics is real-time 1.0x with lively readable motion; no routine whole-film 0.30x/0.38x slow motion. Brief justified slow motion may clarify a critical contact. Judge monotony from playback as well as timing; keep natural acceleration and contact without hidden steering. Release a simple readable setup around 1.0 s. Do not pad to a duration.
Prefer an honest natural loop when the story supports one: show the complete payoff before a visibly powered return, preserve the same object and causal trajectory, and match the camera, mechanism, lighting and audio to the opening. Review two consecutive playbacks. Never hide a failed ending, teleport or substitute the object to close a loop. The loop is optional, not yet a proven audience advantage.
For a looping construction, the 200 ms release rule supersedes the ordinary 1 s opening. Review end-plus-start pacing together; trim redundant lead-in with all audio in sync. Preserve real-time physics, the complete payoff and the continuous powered return. Episode 003 current trim: 9.2 s, revision 16.
avoid: Random viral compilations; gaming/news/politics mixed into this identity; dialogue; filler; excessive flashing; simultaneous stickers/reactions/gameplay; unexplained opening images; missing finals; deceptive loops; object swaps/morphs masquerading as real mechanics; unclear-source downloads; unlicensed platform music; fabricated science or algorithm promises; publication outside the authorized workflow or invented account links. Also avoid predictable orientation-only puzzles with no meaningful obstacle; beauty-shot openings; long identical easing curves; repeated equivalent failures; forced physics outcomes; extra motion without information; padding a simple solution to a target duration.
learnings:
Initial owner-supplied direction adopted on 14 September 2026. The pilot tests a wordless spatial solution using original animation. The owner approved and published the pilot at 2026-09-14T18:50:04Z and subsequently authorized ongoing evening production and publication. Human audience comprehension testing has not been documented. Early public metrics are observations, not validated format learnings; do not infer performance from one film. Experiment definitions and evaluation windows are in examples/turnwise/YOUTUBE_EXPERIMENT.md.

Capture time, exact video age, percentage denominator, public views and likes are not established by this screenshot. Preserve as a separate early observation, not a 24 h or completion measurement. Evidence: examples/turnwise/out/editorial-2026-09-15/owner-observation.json.
Editorial assessment: the pilot has an easily predicted orientation change, a 5.8 s rotation (5.0–10.8 s) and movement without a visible actuator. These are actionable creative weaknesses, not proven causes of the observed rate. The earlier draft score does not establish viewer interest. Owner-requested v2 direction prioritises a stronger visible problem, meaningful progress and causal motion; physics is a hypothesis to test, not a performance finding. Full guidance: examples/turnwise/GENERATION_RULES.md. Never infer poor completion from low stayed-to-watch when retention is unavailable.

15 September 2026 — owner feedback after viewing episode 002, One drop clears the wall: physics and dynamics look substantially better, but the opening should show the full problem early enough to predict or wonder about the outcome. Adopt full_problem_first for future productions: start, relevant route/obstacle, destination and necessary cause before the decisive trigger, usually within the first 2–3 s. Preserve meaningful tension; no mandatory twist or fixed three-second pause. This is qualitative owner feedback and an editorial hypothesis, not evidence that audience engagement improved. No new audience-performance measurements accompany this feedback.
